g.text: K-Way Merge, and the Atomic Segment Swap
Left: merging pre-sorted per-shard results. Right: why a query never sees a half-built index.
A query reading mid-build sees v1
in full, or v2 in full after the swap --
The swap is a single atomic pointer update -- the only synchronization point. Reads never lock; the indexer bears the coordination cost, not queries.
